Panel local projections with fixed effects and clustered errors

Source: R/lp-panel.R
lp_panel.Rd

For a panel \((i,t)\), estimates for each horizon $$y_{i,t+h} = \alpha_{i,h} + \delta_{t,h} + \beta_h s_{it} + \sum_{l=1}^{L}(\phi_{l,h} y_{i,t-l} + \psi_{l,h}s_{i,t-l}) + \kappa_h' x_{it} + e_{i,t+h}$$ by within (demeaning) estimation with unit effects \(\alpha_i\), time effects \(\delta_t\), both, or neither. With two-way effects on an unbalanced horizon sample the demeaning is iterated (alternating projections), a single pass for balanced panels, so no dummy matrix is ever built. Standard errors cluster on the unit (or time) with the Stata-type small-sample correction \(\frac{G}{G-1}\frac{n-1}{n-k}\), \(k\) counting the regressors and the absorbed effects (identical to lm with dummies and hand-coded cluster scores). The joint cross-horizon cluster covariance (scores of a cluster summed over time, stacked over horizons) is returned for lp_supt().

Usage

lp_panel(
  data,
  y,
  shock,
  unit,
  time,
  horizon = 8L,
  lags = 1L,
  controls = NULL,
  fe = c("twoway", "unit", "time", "none"),
  cluster = c("unit", "time"),
  cumulative = FALSE,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9)
)

Arguments

data

a data frame in long format.

y, shock, unit, time

<tidy-select> the columns of the outcome, the shock, the unit id and the time index (regularly spaced).

horizon

maximum horizon.

lags

number of lags of y and shock among the controls.

controls

<tidy-select> further (contemporaneous) control columns.

fe

"twoway", "unit", "time" or "none" (common intercept).

cluster

"unit" or "time".

cumulative

cumulate the outcome over the horizon.

level

confidence levels.

Value

an lp_panel object with $estimate, $se, $bands ((H+1) x 1), $vcov, $nobs, $nclusters.

Details

Economic intuition. Panels (countries, states, firms) give identification and power: unit effects remove time-invariant heterogeneity and time effects remove common shocks, so the response is identified from cross-sectional differences in exposure to \(s\). Clustering by unit allows arbitrary serial correlation within the unit, which is essential because the LP residual is an MA(\(h\)) process. Pitfalls: fixed effects with lagged dependent variables induce Nickell bias when \(T\) is small (use long panels or drop y lags); time effects absorb the average response, so the estimate is a relative effect; with few clusters (< 30) the cluster-robust bands are too narrow; heterogeneous responses are averaged with variance weights.

See also

Other local projections: autoplot.lpm(), compare_lp_var(), lp(), lp_forecast(), lp_joint(), lp_smooth(), lp_state(), lp_supt(), tidy.lpm()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- expand.grid(id = 1:20, t = 1:40)
d$s <- rnorm(nrow(d))
d$y <- 0.5 * d$s + rnorm(nrow(d))
lp_panel(d, y, s, id, t, horizon = 3, lags = 1)$estimate
#>              y
#> 0  0.550833521
#> 1  0.076868592
#> 2 -0.006838165
#> 3  0.036043860
